item.title: European Parliament rejects China’s pressure on Taiwan, calls for closer EU-Taiwan Ties

item.content:encoded:
European Parliament rejects China’s pressure on Taiwan, calls for closer EU-Taiwan Ties The European Parliament has adopted a recommendation rejecting China’s efforts to restrict Taiwan’s participation in international organisations and exchanges, while calling for stronger economic, technological and security cooperation between the European Union and Taiwan, Taipei Times reported. ANI | Updated: 09-10-2026 17:12 IST | Created: 09-10-2026 17:12 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The European Parliament has adopted a recommendation rejecting China’s efforts to restrict Taiwan’s participation in international organisations and exchanges, while calling for stronger economic, technological and security cooperation between the European Union and Taiwan, Taipei Times reported. According to Taipei Times, the recommendation, adopted on Wednesday, was addressed to the European Council, European Commission and European Union foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas. It described Taiwan as a valuable partner in trade and technology and highlighted the strategic importance of closer relations between the two sides. The European Parliament opposed what it called China’s attempts to pressure international organisations, third countries and other actors into limiting Taiwan’s international participation and contacts. The recommendation cited Chinese pressure over Taiwan Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim’s participation in a European Parliament-organised conference on freedom and democracy last month, Taipei Times reported. The recommendation also expressed strong disapproval of China’s alleged transnational repression activities, including an investigation into Taiwanese legislator Puma Shen under a 2024 judicial guideline accusing him of promoting separatism through the civil defence organisation Kuma Academy. Reaffirming the European Union’s longstanding “one China” policy, the recommendation clarified that the bloc has never endorsed Beijing’s own “one China” principle. It also opposed any unilateral attempt to alter the cross-strait status quo through force, coercion or actions against the will of the Taiwanese people, according to Taipei Times. The parliament urged the European Union and its regional democratic partners to strengthen security coordination, maintain a continuous naval presence and conduct joint exercises to support regional stability. It also called on the European Commission to pursue measures aimed at deterring China from escalating tensions with Taiwan. On the international front, lawmakers urged the United Nations to reject Chinese demands restricting Republic of China passport holders’ access to its tours and events. They also opposed Beijing’s interpretation of United Nations Resolution 2758 as supporting its sovereignty claims over Taiwan, noting that the resolution concerns China’s representation at the United Nations and does not mention Taiwan. According to Taipei Times, the recommendation further called for deeper cooperation with Taiwan in semiconductors and cybersecurity, alongside preparations for negotiations on a bilateral investment agreement or an alternative arrangement covering critical supply chains. (ANI)

item.title: US Fed's Waller expects more rate hikes as inflation stays elevated
item.description: US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller has indicated that further interest rate hikes are likely in the coming months as inflation remains stubbornly above the central bank's 2 per cent target ...
item.content:encoded:
US Fed's Waller expects more rate hikes as inflation stays elevated US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller has indicated that further interest rate hikes are likely in the coming months as inflation remains stubbornly above the central bank's 2 per cent target, although the timing and pace of increases will depend on incoming economic data. ANI | Updated: 09-10-2026 14:59 IST | Created: 09-10-2026 14:59 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller has indicated that further interest rate hikes are likely in the coming months as inflation remains stubbornly above the central bank's 2 per cent target, although the timing and pace of increases will depend on incoming economic data. Speaking at the Istanbul Economic Forum in Türkiye on Thursday, Waller said the US economy remains resilient enough to withstand tighter monetary policy, while persistent price pressures continue to pose risks to inflation control. "If the economic data continue to come in as expected, I anticipate additional hikes to support a timelier return of inflation to our 2 percent goal," Waller said. However, he clarified that the central bank does not necessarily need to raise rates at every policy meeting. "The hikes do not need to come at consecutive meetings, but they should be in place in an acceptable period of time," he added. His remarks come after the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points in September to a range of 3.75-4 per cent, ending a nine-month period of unchanged rates. Waller said the decision to resume tightening was driven by several months of economic evidence rather than a single inflation reading. He pointed to a stable labour market and persistent inflationary pressures, including elevated energy prices, the expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure and uncertainty surrounding global trade. "Instead, it was a preponderance of evidence over several months that the risks for monetary policy had shifted, reflecting a strengthened labor market and a range of persistent inflationary forces," he said. Waller noted that the ongoing Middle East conflict had contributed to high energy prices, while damaged infrastructure and low inventories could keep oil prices elevated through 2027. He also highlighted the inflationary impact of expanding artificial intelligence infrastructure, saying evidence had mounted that the AI buildout was significantly driving up high-tech consumer prices. Continuing trade conflicts and the possibility of additional tariffs could also put renewed upward pressure on inflation, he indicated. On the latest economic data, Waller said US core personal consumption expenditures inflation stood at 3 per cent annually in August, remaining above the Fed's target. "Overall, the new data reinforce my view that the labor market is stable and inflation is too high. For at least the near term, policy will be focused on the inflation side of our mandate," he said. He also expressed confidence that tighter monetary policy would not significantly damage economic growth. "I am not greatly concerned that tighter monetary policy threatens a damaging slowdown in the economy," Waller said, citing signs of strengthening economic activity in the second half of 2026. On the outlook for further tightening, Waller highlighted the Fed's September economic projections, which showed that 16 of 18 policymakers expected at least one additional interest rate hike during the remaining two meetings of 2026. Four of them anticipated two more increases. He said financial markets were also pricing in further tightening, with futures indicating an 85 per cent probability of at least one rate hike by the December meeting, based on prices as of October 7. Waller emphasised that the Fed's economic projections help communicate the likely direction of monetary policy without committing policymakers to a fixed path. "Simply put, policymakers could signal where they are likely headed while acknowledging that there is no fixed final destination—except for the achievement of price stability and maximum employment," he said. His remarks suggest that while further US monetary tightening remains likely, the pace of future increases will depend on whether inflation shows meaningful signs of returning towards the Federal Reserve's target. (ANI)

item.description: Young doctors at the Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre (JPMC) in Karachi staged a protest over the non-payment of their salaries for three consecutive months, accusing the hospital administration and ...
item.content:encoded:
Pakistan: JPMC doctors protest as salary crisis exposes Sindh’s administrative failure Young doctors at the Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre (JPMC) in Karachi staged a protest over the non-payment of their salaries for three consecutive months, accusing the hospital administration and the Sindh government of failing to resolve the issue, as reported by The Express Tribune. ANI | Updated: 09-10-2026 14:49 IST | Created: 09-10-2026 14:49 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Young doctors at the Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre (JPMC) in Karachi staged a protest over the non-payment of their salaries for three consecutive months, accusing the hospital administration and the Sindh government of failing to resolve the issue, as reported by The Express Tribune. According to The Express Tribune, the protesting doctors assembled outside the Outpatient Department (OPD) Complex and raised slogans against the hospital administration. They said they had continued treating patients and performing their duties despite receiving no salaries, while authorities repeatedly shifted responsibility for the delay between different offices. The doctors said they had effectively been caught between the hospital administration and the provincial government. Hospital officials directed them towards the Sindh government, while government officials referred the matter back to the hospital administration. The salary crisis followed a change introduced by the Sindh government in May in the payment mechanism for house officers. Under the previous system, hospitals received funds and paid doctors through bank cheques. The revised procedure requires salaries to be transferred directly into doctors’ bank accounts. Officials said the new mechanism required additional documentation, including copies of doctors’ CNICs and information concerning previous payments, which had to be submitted to the Sindh Accountant General (AG) office. Sindh Young Doctors Association President Dr Shahid Awan stated that the doctors would intensify their protest if their pending salaries were not released within the next few days. He warned that demonstrations could be expanded to the hospital administration block and surrounding roads. The protesting doctors also demanded an increase in their salaries, claiming they had not received a raise since 2020, as cited by The Express Tribune. Meanwhile, the Sindh Health Department had earlier rejected allegations of negligence by the hospital administration. In a September 30 statement, it attributed the delay to the implementation of the new direct-payment system and the process of establishing vendor accounts at the AG office, as reported by The Express Tribune. (ANI)
